From: Elena Torres <elena@hyperbyte.io>

Cc: 
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexplained mid-cycle usage spike and VAT on Invoice HB-889

Hi Michael,

We just received Invoice #HB-889 for the billing period Jul 25 - Aug 8 and noticed a large mid-cycle usage spike (line items show ~142k tokens between Aug 2-4). The total is significantly above our historical baseline and includes VAT charged twice in two separate line items: one for usage and another labeled "regional tax adjustment."

Can you help explain the origin of the spike and confirm whether VAT was applied correctly? Our AP team is pausing payment on the disputed portion (~$12,430) while we get clarification. Payment on the undisputed balance will proceed as scheduled.

Attached: invoice-HB-889.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Director of Finance
HyperByte


-----

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the stress. I see the invoice and the spike on our end as well.

Quick plan:
- I'm pulling the per-key/per-route usage export for Aug 1–8 and will share a CSV within 48 hours.
- I'll ask Billing (cc'd Ben) to check VAT line item generation to confirm whether the "regional tax adjustment" was double-counted.
- As a gesture of good faith while we investigate, we can provisionally credit up to 50% of the disputed amount pending root-cause. If we find an internal attribution error we will credit the full disputed amount.

Two asks from you:
1) Please confirm whether you want us to pause collection on the disputed $12,430 portion (we can put that on hold in our invoicing system).
2) If possible, share the AP contact name/phone so our collections team can coordinate.

I'll follow up by EOD Tue with the export and a preliminary breakdown.

Best,

Subject: internal: HyperByte HB-889 mid-cycle spike (need per-key attribution)

Grace / Ben — forwarding Elena's note. Initial triage notes below.

Why I suspect duplicate attribution:
- The usage waterfall shows multiple high-throughput embedding calls between Aug 2 02:00 and Aug 4 11:00 UTC, aligned with an automated reindex job HyperByte ran last week.
- We see the same request IDs replayed across two model routes in our logs which may have caused attribution to two separate billing buckets.

Ben: can you run the per-API-key attribution export for Aug 1–8 (granularity: 1h) and include the raw request-id column. Focus on keys associated with HyperByte (account HB-2025-42). Export name: redwood-usage-export-20260801-20260808.csv
Grace: if there is a customer-facing anomaly we should offer a partial credit and update the customer success ticket. I'm fine with the provisional 50% credit but would like Billing to sign off before we finalize.

I'll draft the customer-facing breakdown once Ben provides the CSV.

Thanks — Michael

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle usage spike + VAT allocation question - HyperByte (Invoice HB-889)

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience. Attached is the per-key usage export and our audit notes. Key points below.

Summary of findings
- Root cause: a scheduled embedding reindex job executed Aug 2 02:03 UTC using a legacy API key that had been copied into two ingestion hosts. Due to an internal routing configuration edge-case, a subset of requests were routed to both the "ingest-standard" and "ingest-high-threshold" billing routes, causing duplicated attribution for ~49,600 tokens.
- VAT: we incorrectly generated a separate "regional tax adjustment" line in addition to VAT on usage for that duplicated portion. That should not have happened.

Actions & remediation
- We've attached: redwood-usage-export-20260801-20260808.csv (per-key, per-request-id) and a short audit doc.
- We are issuing a credit for the duplicated usage plus the misapplied VAT. Proposed credit: $6,215. This equals the duplicated-charge portion plus reclaimed VAT; the net disputed balance remaining would be $6,215 (from original ~$12,430).
- If HyperByte prefers the full hold, we can place the entire disputed amount on hold while we finalize the credit memo (but we expect the root cause makes a full credit likely).

Next steps for you
1) Confirm you want us to apply the provisional credit $6,215 now, or hold the full disputed $12,430 until we finalize the credit memo.
2) If approved, we'll send a DocuSign credit memo and update invoice HB-889 to reflect the adjustment (expect updated invoice within 24 hours).

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-usage-export-20260801-20260808.csv (CSV, 56KB)], [attachment: proposed-credit-memo-HB-889.pdf (PDF, 22KB)]

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 | Credit memo preview: https://app.redwood.ai/credits/CM-HB-889

Apologies again for the noise — we'll follow up with a short post-mortem and the preventive config change (block duplicate route mapping for legacy keys).

Best regards,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
